newsitem.title: USA: Humana to cut as many as 900 jobs nationwide.
newsitem.headline: Humana to cut as many as 900 jobs nationwide.

text.p: Humana Inc. said Monday it will cut up to 900 jobs nationwide next year, or as much as 5 percent of its work force, and take a pretax charge of about $15 million for the move.
The company, one of the largest managed health care companies in the United States, currently employs 18,000 people across the country.
The charge, to be taken in the fourth quarter, amounts to $10 million after tax, or 6 cents a share, the company said.
"The marketplace ... demands that we be as efficient as possible and that our administrative expenses be in line," said Humana President Gregory Wolf.
"Furthermore, the savings created by this action will offset a portion of the investment needed to achieve long-term efficiencies in the areas of information systems and medical management," he said.
Humana is based in Louisville, Ky.
